column2: One should place the nine syllables of the vidya in the nine openings of the body, and perform the pervading placement with the whole, for one's own perfection.
In all the vidyas one should perform the pervading placement. [Meditate on her] like molten gold, beautiful in fresh youth,
her lotus face lovely with a smile, her three eyes shining, with eight arms, radiant with ruby ornaments,
her garments reddened by the rays of her ruby crown, clad in yellow silk, with jewelled anklets and girdle,
shining with clusters of red pearls; holding in her left hands a jewelled lotus, a conch, a sugarcane bow and the full orb of the moon,
and in her right hands a kahlara lotus, a golden horn, a flower arrow and a citron,
surrounded on all sides by Shaktis bearing their own names. Meditating thus, one should worship Vahnivasini, whose form is fire,
by whose remembrance the three worlds come under control. Now the seventh Nitya, Mahavajreshvari, O sage —
I will tell her vidya, which grants great success to practitioners: the second of Vahnivasini, the fourth of Nityaklinna,
the fifth, the first of Bhagamala, the second of Bherunda, the second of Nityaklinna, the third, sixth and seventh,
the eighth and ninth, and again the first and last; two, one, one, then two and two, then two —
enclosing them with Maya, one should perform the six limbs in order, and place the ten letters of the mantra, each enclosed with Shakti,
on the eyes, ears, nose, speech, chest, navel and private parts in order. [Meditate on her,] red, in red garments, adorned with red perfumes and garlands,
four-armed, three-eyed, radiant with a ruby crown, holding noose, goad, sugarcane bow and pomegranate-flower arrow
in her arms, gazing at the practitioner with eyes cool with compassion and love, in the weapon, hexagon, lotus and earth-square,
seated at ease in the middle of the chakra, her lotus face smiling, surrounded by Shaktis of her own form, in the middle of a yellow [seat],
on a lion-throne, surrounded by Shaktis in rocking boats all around, always playing with them in coming and going and the like,
in an ocean of red — so should one contemplate the queen of the mantra. This is declared the seventh; hear now of the eighth, Duti.
The first of Vajreshvari is first, then Viyat with Agni, then Ambu with Maruta, then Gotra with Kshma,
then Raya with Vyasa and Shuchi; the last letter of Vahnivasini — thus is declared the Nitya Duti.
With the vidya joined to the six long vowels one makes the six limbs; with letters enclosed by that same, one should place them on the five beginning with the ears,
placing the sixth on the nose, and perform the pervading placement with the vidya. [Meditate on her] radiant as the midday sun in the hot season,
with a crown of the nine gems, three-eyed, in red garments, her body shining with the lustre of many ornaments,
smiling brightly, eight-armed, praised by the great sages, holding in her left hands noose, shield, mace and a jewelled cup,
and in her right a goad, sword, dagger and lotus, eager to grant the practitioner's wishes.
Meditating thus, one should worship the Goddess Duti, destroyer of bad policy. Thus she has been told to you, who wards off all calamities,
brings prosperity, grants dwelling in Shiva-hood and gives all success. Now, Narada, I will tell you the ninth Nitya, named Tvarita,
who grants fame, learning, wealth, health and happiness. The first of Vahnivasini, then the first of Duti,
Hamsa with Dhara and Sva, Tejas with Chara, Vayu with Prabha and Chara, with Grasa and Shakti,
the heart with Raya and Daha, Vahni and Sva as the eighth, Hamsa with Kshma and Kha, Grasa with Chara as the second,
the second with nada — this is the twelve-syllable Nitya Tvarita. With seven syllables beginning from the fourth letter of the vidya,
one should make the limbs with pairs of letters, six in order, on hands and body; on the head, forehead, throat, heart, navel and base,
the two thighs, the two knees, the two shanks and the two feet one should place the ten letters of the mantra,
with the letters of the mantra from the second, the penultimate and the middle, and the others too, beginning with Tara. Hear her meditation, which brings all success:
dark in colour, of auspicious form, beautiful in fresh youth, radiant with ornaments made of eight serpents, two by two —
earrings, armlets, girdle and anklets of serpents of the brahmin, kshatriya, vaishya and shudra kinds, of fearsome form —
clad in garments of leaves, her arms adorned with fine bracelets of peacock feathers, shining with a ruby crown,
with a chaplet of peacock feathers, an umbrella and banner of the same, her chest shining with strings of gunja berries, her breasts marked with saffron,
three-eyed, lovely of face, her lotus face gently smiling, her four arms shining with noose, goad, boon and fearlessness.
Meditating thus on the Goddess Totala, one should worship her surrounded by Shaktis; before her stands Phatkari, radiant with arrow and bow in hand,
who is pleased to grant fruit quickly to practitioners. This ninth Nitya is called Tvarita, O lord of sages,
who quells obstacles and bad dreams and grants every wish. Shuchi with Sva is first, joined with Rasa and Vahni;
Prana with Sva is second, the other with Vanat and the Shaktis — thus is declared the three-syllable Nitya Kulasundari,
by whose mere remembrance omniscience arises. With those three root letters one should perform the six limbs,
at the beginning, middle and end, in the order of worship and japa; with each of those three seeds joined with the long vowels
one should perform the placement on the hands, body and face as prescribed; with the upward, eastern, southern, northern, western and downward faces,
placed in order in the intervals, in their own natures; one on the base, crown and heart, the second on the three eyes,
the third on the ears and chin, the fourth on the nose and palate, the fifth on the shoulders and navel, then on the hands and feet,
at root, middle and tip, one should place them ninefold with the root letters. [Meditate on her,] red, served by a host of red Shaktis,
with red garments, ornaments, garlands and unguents, with six lotus faces, radiant with a ruby crown set with priceless gems,
auspicious, her breast shining with clusters of jewels, supreme in compassion and bliss, seated on a red lotus,
twelve-armed, the essence of all speech for all; holding a coral rosary, a lotus, a jewelled water-pot,
a cup full of gems, a citron and the teaching gesture in her right hands, and in her left a book and a red lotus,
a golden pen, a jewelled garland and an excellent conch; praised all around by gods, Gandharvas and Kinnaras,
Yakshas, Rakshasas, Daityas, sages, Siddhas, Vidyadharas and others. Meditating thus, one should worship the Nitya for success in speech, prosperity and beauty.
One should remember her as white for success in speech alone, golden for prosperity, smoke-coloured for enmity among foes, for death and for restraint,
and blue for striking dumb — according to what is needed. Thus this tenth Nitya, Kulasundari, has been told to you.
Now I will tell of the eleventh, Nityanitya, Trikuta. Hamsa, joined with the heart, Prana, Rasa, Daha and Karna,
joined by tradition with the vidya of Kulasundari — this is Nityanitya of three letters, joined with six kuta syllables,
held to have seventy-two variations by reverse order and other forms; by worshipping her a man becomes perfected, a sky-rover and happy,
able to restrain and to favour in the three worlds. The six limbs are made with Hamsa and the heart joined with the long vowels.
Between the brows, at the throat, heart, navel, private parts and base in order, one should place the letters of the vidya, joined with the dot,
and having performed the pervading placement with the whole duly, one should meditate on Shiva, the Self of all, for the sake of all prosperity:
radiant as the rising sun's orb, shining with a ruby crown, adorned with rubies, wearing red garments,
resplendent with six lotus faces shining with lovely smiles, three eyes in each face, with twelve arms,
holding in her left hands noose, rosary, pundra sugarcane bow, shield and trident, and a goad and a book,
and in her right hands a flower arrow, a lotus, a human skull and the gesture of fearlessness — one should meditate on the Goddess with undivided mind.
Thus the eleventh has been told; hear, Narada, of the twelfth. The first is the last of Tvarita, with Dyuti, Daha, Chara and Sva,
the heart with Daha, Kshma and Sva, and the fifth of Vajreshi; Marut with Sva, with the middle; and again after the tenth,
Bhumi with Rasa, Kshma and Sva, then the eighth of Vajreshi in order; six syllables of Tvarita, the third next,
Dyuti with Daha, Chara and Sva, then the first of this — thus is declared the seventeen-syllable Nitya called Nilapataka.
The limbs are formed with two, two, two, two, two and six letters from the mantra; on the ears, the two nostrils, speech, throat and heart in order,
at the navel, base and the joints of the feet in order one should place all seventeen letters of the mantra,
and perform the pervading placement with the whole as prescribed. [Meditate on her] like a sapphire, shining with a crown of brilliant gems,
five-faced, three-eyed, in red garments, ten-armed, adorned with ornaments of gleaming pearls and gems,
her body rich with clusters of jewels, her face lovely with a smile; holding noose, banner, shield, Sharnga bow and boon
in her left hands, adorned with all ornaments, and goad, spear, sword, arrow and fearlessness
in her right hands, seated on a lotus seat, surrounded by hosts of Shaktis like herself in colour, dress, faces, hands, weapons and ornaments —
so one should meditate on the Goddess in the daily worship. A lotus with triangle and hexagon, eight petals, outside it
an octagon enclosed by two earth-squares, a pair of those cities with four gates in the directions and with branches —
making this, one should worship Shiva there with the Shaktis named in the enclosures. This twelfth Nitya, Nilapatakini, has been told to you,
granting victory in battle and success with the sword, sandals and collyrium; bringing vetalas, yakshinis, servants, pishachas and the like under control,
gaining treasures, caves and perfected food, impelled by desire. Now, Narada, I will tell of the thirteenth Nitya; listen.
Rasa, Nabha, Daha, Vyapta, Kshma and Vana first, joined with Kha — this is the single-syllable Nitya Vijaya, O sage.
With the consonants of the vidya joined with long vowels one should make four limbs, and two with the remaining ones, on hands and body.
On the senses of knowledge beginning with the ears and on the mind one should place the letters in order, joined with the dot; the rest as before.
[Meditate on her,] five-faced, ten-armed, three-eyed in each face, radiant with the crescent moon set in her brilliant crown,
endowed with all ornaments, resplendent in yellow garments, her bodily lustre like the rising sun's orb, brightly smiling,
holding in her left arms conch, noose, shield, bow and kahlara lotus, and discus, goad, sword, arrow and citron
in her right hands; terrible to behold in applications, gentle in worship, seated on a lion,
surrounded by Shaktis riding tigers; seated at ease in battle, worship and other applications;
and in worship the Shaktis too are seated at ease, all like the Goddess in form, faces, hands and weapons.
Making two squares adorned with four gates and furnished with eight branches, one should worship there as before;
within that, making an octagon within two circles, and within that a lotus with sixteen petals,
and likewise an eight-petalled lotus, one should invoke her there and worship her properly with offerings, surrounded by her Shaktis.
This thirteenth is declared, granting victory in debate and battle. Now I will tell of the fourteenth Nitya, Sarvamangala.
Kha joined with the heart, Ambu and Vana — this is the Nitya Sarvamangala.
Perfected by this single-syllable one, a man at once becomes a sky-rover. One should place the root vidya with the six long vowels on the six limbs.
[Meditate on] that Nitya, golden in colour, adorned with pearls and rubies, with a ruby crown, compassion rippling in her two eyes,
two-armed, commanding, on a lotus with eight and sixteen petals, in a pair of earth-houses with four gates,
holding a citron in her right lotus hand, and with her left granting wealth and the like to her devotees,
surrounded on all sides by Shaktis like herself, and accompanied by seventy-six others born of the Apsaras;
at other times in applications, always with the Shaktis described in the worship. This fourteenth has been told; hear now of the fifteenth.
Bhu, Shunya with Nabha, Bhu and Rasa, then Sthira and Ambu, Raya with Agni, Jya with Ambu and Marut, Rasa and Marut,
Nabha with Maruta, Rasa joined with Shunya, Gotra with Chara, and the letter before Ambu,
Ambu, Agni and the heart, Daha, Ambu, Rasa, Kshma, Raya and the heart with Sva; Hamsa with Maruta, Daha, and Prana with Maruta,
Daha with Agni, Prana and Chara, Raya with Jya and Marut, Ambu with Chara, Gotra, the heart with Agni, Jya, Ambu and Rasa with Sva,
Raya with Agni, Jya, Ambu and Rasa — these again, then Javi; with this Daha they become double; Bhasva with Daha, Marut and Sva,
Hamsa with Daha, Vahni and Sva, and he with Daha, Kshma and Sva; then seven Dahas, and five beginning with the eighth,
that below the penultimate, after Nilapataka, [letters of] Tvarita, and the eighth and ninth of Bherunda —
this is the Nitya Jvalamalini, declared of sixty-three syllables. With one, two, four, five, four and ten letters
of the root, from the beginning, one should make the six limbs on hands and body, and the pervading placement with the rest; then meditate on the eternal one:
like blazing fire, radiant with a ruby crown, six-faced, twelve-armed, adorned with all ornaments,
holding in her lotus hands noose and goad, sword and shield, bow and arrow, mace and conch, trident and fire, boon and fearlessness,
surrounded on all sides by Shaktis of her own measure, her lotus face shining with a lovely smile, with three eyes.
Meditating thus, one should worship her daily with those offerings. Making two squares with four gates,
an eight-petalled lotus with branches, within it a triangle, then a hexagon, and a triangle in the middle — one should worship Shiva there.
This fifteenth has been told; hear, Narada, of the sixteenth: Chitra, of two syllables formed from Vayu, the pranava and the principles,
who, when perfected, is employed for gaining wealth, grain and treasure. With the first Vayu of the vidya joined with the long vowels in order
one should make the six limbs as before, and place the alphabet with the vidya. [Meditate on her] like the rising sun's orb, adorned with the nine gems,
with a crown of the nine gems, shining in bright silk, four-armed, three-eyed, her face shining with a bright smile,
the eternal one full of all bliss, granting every wish; holding in her four hands noose, goad, boon and fearlessness,
auspicious, in the middle of the triangle in the lotus pericarp; with her Shaktis in her chakra, worship is declared in the same way.
Prana and Daha with Dhara, again the first, Marut in Rasa, Vyasa with Marut and Shakti, Bhu with Sva, then the three;
her first, a pair of Rasas joined with Charana, Hamsa joined with Daha and the Shaktis of Vahni, then after that
Nabha, the heart with Daha, Ambu, Jya, and Shunya with Sva; then Ambu with Visha, with Maruta and Nabha,
Shunya and Vyapta with Bhu, Hamsa — the first and last are the three mantras; the first is declared as the five letters from her sixth,
the second section declared as the last from the eleven-syllable one, the third of twenty-five syllables — so the mantras are told in order.
Bala, with the three seeds and the rest, with mantras twice and thrice, makes the six limbs. [Meditate on her] with scattered locks, naked, red, of blissful form,
holding in her hands arrow, bow, noose and goad; and the goddesses too, of like weapons, form and colour,
having bathed after their season, ... their eyes always red with bliss. Thus Kurukulla and Chandravali herself have been declared.
I will now speak of Varahi, the supreme body of Lalita. Shuchi with Sva, then Shunya, Sthira with Nabha, Abhra and Rasa,
then Ambu, Raya with Agni, and Ambu and Raya with Marut, Agni with Ila — these again joined with Ambu and Marut,
Hamsa with Daha, Ambu and Maruta, and these three again with Agni; Ambu and Daha with Marut, then Hamsa, Nabha with Dhara,
five again with Tejas and Agni, Vata with Sva, Toya with Chara before it, then Toya with Agni,
Shunya with Vyapta and Shuchi, Shunya with Shakti and Nabha, Daha, Dhara with Sva, Toya with Chara —
this is declared the former part; after this a group of four: joined with the one called Jya, with Chara, and Rabha before it,
Rasa again with Agni; the fourfold group, then ... with Chara too, Hamsa with Sva before it,
Hamsa with Agni, the three before, the heart with Sva; Rasa with Chara before it, and Rasa joined with Agni,
the three declared after, Vata with Dhara and Nabha; Prana with Sva, then Rasa with the heart and Sva,
these three pervaded, then Ambu with Daha; Gotra with Bhara, Sparsha with nada and Javi,
with Daha, each before and the former with Maruta; Shunya with Marut and Sva, the heart with Daha, Ambu and Chara,
Sparsha with Marut and Sva, the heart with Daha and Ambu; Jya and Agni with Sva, Hamsa, and Ambu with Maruta,
the heart with Rupa and Sva, and Rasa with Sva; Prana and Daha with Dhara, and these again with Vahni and Viyat,
Ambu with Var and Daha, with ... and Sva; the two letters repeated before, and Shuddhi with Sva likewise,
Sthira, Rasa ... with Sva, two Davas and Hamsas, Dhara with Sva; Yuti with nada, then the heart with Ambu and Maruta,
and Hamsa with Maruta — the vidya of one hundred and ten syllables. Varahi, Panchami, Vishvavijaya, Bhadrakaumudi,
and famed as Vartali, granting all wishes such as paralysis. One should make the limbs with the letters of the mantra — seven, six,
ten, seven and seven, with the jatis. Making a chakra with triangle, circle, hexagon and two circles,
and writing her name there, one should worship; then meditate on the Goddess with the face of a boar, golden in colour,
a woman in form up to the neck, [her face] like a blazing tawny lotus, three-eyed and eight-armed, [holding] discus, conch and goad,
noose, pestle, a head, fearlessness and boon — one should contemplate her seated at ease on Garuda's shoulder.
In the daily worship, O sage, one should remember her Shaktis as like her; in applications one should remember the Goddess seated on a lion or riding a tiger,
riding an elephant, a horse or Tarkshya, with her Shaktis; dark, red, yellow or of blue-lotus form,
one should meditate on her so in the various applications to attain the various aims: one should remember Panchami as red for control, yellow for paralysis,
dark on a difficult road, white in battle for the destruction of enemies, and smoke-coloured for driving away — so the practitioner should meditate, best of brahmins.
These sixteen Nityas have been declared to you in brief; they grant wishes at once to those who worship them and destroy all sins.
Prapti, Prakamya, Ishita and Vashita, Bhukti, Siddhi and likewise Iccha — [the Goddess] is declared to be the form of the siddhis.
Brahmi, Maheshvari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Indrani, Chamunda, in the form of Mahalakshmi,
Kama, Buddhi, Ahamkara, in the form of sound and touch, the form of form, called Rasa, Gandha, Vitta and Dhriti,
called Nabha, Bija and Amrita, in the form of memory, body and self; Kusuma, Mekhala, Madana, Madanatura,
Rekha, Samvegini, Ankusha and Malini, Samkshobhini, Vidravini, in the form of Akarshana,
declared as Ahladini and Sammohini, Stambhini, Jambhini, Vashankari and Ranjini,
Unmadini and likewise proclaimed Arthasadhini; full of prosperity, made of mantra, destroyer of the pairs,
Siddhi, giver of prosperity, bringer of dear blessings, called giver of desires, and releaser from sorrow,
calmer of death, remover of obstacles, Angasundarika and giver of good fortune,
giver of knowledge and lordship, made of knowledge, the fifth; dwelling in the Vindhya, of terrible form, remover of sins,
full of bliss, protection, granting the fruit desired in form; Jayini, Vimala, Kameshi, Vajrini, Bhaga,
the stations called Trailokyamohana and Sarvashaparipurani, abiding in Sarvasamkshobhana, established in Saubhagyaprada,
whose house is Sarvarthasadhaka, abiding in Sarvarogahara, whose station is Sarvarakshakara, abiding in Sarvasiddhiprada,
of Shiva's nature in the bindu-station, the support full of all bliss; Prakrishta, Gupta and Guptatara,
of the form of tradition, dwelling within Kula and Kaula, secret, beyond the high and low, Prakrit and very secret,
Tripura, Tripureshi and Puravasini, Shrimalini, Siddhanta, Mahatripurasundari,
shining in the island of the nine gems with its nine divisions, dwelling in the garden of wish-trees, worshipped by the seasons and senses,
Kalamudra, called Matrika, teacher of the land of jewels, the image called Tattvagrahaga, and the elephant of sense objects,
of the form of place, time, shape and sound, the yogini of music, joined with the chakra of all secret, manifest and perfected yoginis,
called fire, sun, moon and element, called the eight-syllable Self, of fivefold form to be held, named with many vows,
free from forbidden conduct, of the form of the marks of the perfected, abiding in the four parts of the tortoise, of the form of the daily and other worships,
worshipped with damanaka and the like, granting success in the six rites, bringing good through worship with different substances on lunar days and weekdays,
Vayoshi, Anangakusuma and Anangamekhala, called Anangamadana and Anangamadanatura,
Madavegini and Bhuvanapalini, declared as Shashilekha and held to be called Gatilekha,
Shraddha, Priti, Rati, Dhriti, Kanti, Manorama, called Manohara and Manoratha,
Madanonmadini, Modini, Shankhini, Shoshini, Shankari, Sinjini and Subhaga,
Pusha, Sumanasa, Rati, Priti, Dhriti, Riddhi, Saumya, Marichi and Amshumalini,
Shashini, Angira, Chhaya, Sampurnamandala, Tushti, called Amrita, Dakini and Lokapa,
in the form of Batuka and Ibha, Durga in the form of the lord of the field, in the form of Kamaraja and of Manmatha,
in the form of Kandarpa and of Makaraketana, in the form of Manobhava, Bharati in the form of the letters,
Madana, Mohini, Lila, Jambhini, Udyama, Shubha, Hladini, Dravini, Priti, Rati, Rakta, Manorama,
Sarvonmada, Sarvamukha, Abhanga, Amitodyama, Analpa, of unmanifest glory, of various agitating forms,
the power of attachment and the power of aversion, in the form of sound and the rest; Nitya, Niranjana, Klinna, Kledini, Madanatura,
Madadrava, Dravini and Dravini — so declared; Madavila, Mangala, Manmathani, Manasvini,
Moha, Moda, Manamayi, Maya, Manda, Mitavati, Vijaya, Vimala, Shubha and Vishva,
Vibhuti, Vinata, Vividha, Vinata in order, Kamala, Kamini, Kirata, in the form of Kirti,
declared as Kuttini and likewise Kulasundari, Kalyani, Kalakola, Dakini and Shakini,
Lakini, Kakini, Rakini and Kakini, called Iccha, Jnana and Kriya, bearer of the eight weapons,
declared as Kapardini and likewise Kulasundari, Jvalini, Visphulinga, Mangala, Sumanohara,
Kanaka, Kinava, Vidya and Vividha are declared; Mesha, called Vrisha, Mithuna and Karkata,
Simha, Kanya, Tula, Kita, Chapa and Makara, Kumbha, Mina, Sara and Sarvabhaksha,
declared as the Self of the universe, of wondrous forms arising variously; without rival, without fear, of inconceivable glory beyond asking,
then declared as Rakta, in the form of the attainment of knowledge; Hrillekha, Kledini, Klinna, Kshobhini, Madanatura,
Nispandana, Ragavati and Madanavati, Mekhala, Dravini and Vegavati are declared,
Kamala, Kamini, Kalpa, Kala and Kalitadbhuta, Kirata, Kala, Kadana and Kaushika,
Kambuvadanika, Katara and Kapata, Kirti, Kumari and Kunkuma are declared,
Bhanjini, Vegini, Naga, Chapala, Peshala, Sati, Rati, Shraddha, Bhogalola, Madonmatta, Manasvini,
Vihvala, Karshini, Lola and Madanamalini, Vinoda, Kautuka, Punya and Purana are declared,
Vagishi, Varada, Vishva, Vibhava, Avighnakarini, Bijavighnahara, Vidya, Sumukhi and Sundari,
Sara and Sumana, and declared as Sarasvati, Samaya, Sarvaga, Viddha, Shiva and Vani,
declared as Durasiddha and held to be Vigrahavati, Nada, Manonmani, of the glory of Pranapratishtha and Aruna,
Prana, Apana, Samana, Vyana and Udana are declared; Naga, Kurma, Krikala, Devadatta and Dhananjaya,
Phatkari, worshipped by servants, Jaya and Vijaya, Humkari, Khecari, Chanda, Chhedini and Kshapini,
Strihumkari, Kshemakari, in the form of four syllables, whose limbs are the letters of the doctrine of Shrividya, Kali, Yamya, Nriparnaka,
Bhasha, Sarasvati, Vani, Samskrita and Para, Bahurupa, Chittarupa, Ramyananda and Kautuka,
called Traya and Paramatma, of immeasurable glory, of the nature of speech, of the form of bindu and visarga, and the Self of the universe,
called Traipurakanda, of threefold nature as knower and the rest, giver of long life, prosperity, fame, enjoyment, beauty and health,
declared to be made of knowledge of this world and the next, called Jiva and Vijaya, and made of knowledge of the universe,
the vidyas beginning with the heart, of the forms of radiance beginning with form, the body of the world, Vishvamohanika, called Tripuramrita,
of the form that nourishes all, Mohini, Kshobhini, declared as Kledini and likewise Mahodaya,
Sampatkari, of the letters ha, la and ksha, Sima, the body of the Mothers, Rati, Priti, Manobhava, and declared as Varadhipa,
Trikuta, Shatkuta and Panchakuta, going in the vishuddha, going in the anahata, abiding in the manipuraka,
seated in the svadhishthana, abiding in the base and in the ajna, of the form of thirty-six kutas, of the nature of the fifty pairs,
queen of the siddhis beginning with the sandals, giver of victory, giver of the power to change form, in the form of a vetala, and a pishachi,
Vichitra, Vibhrama, Hamsi, Bhishani, Janaranjika, Vishala, Madana, Tushta, Kalakanthi, Mahabhaya,
Mahendri, Shankhini, Aindri, Mangala, Vatavasini, Mekhala, Sakala, Lakshmi, Malini, Vishvanayika,
Sulochana, Sushobha, Kamada and Vilasini, Kameshvari, Nandini, Svarnarekha, Manohara,
Pramoda, Ragini, Siddha, Padmini and Ratipriya, Kalyanada, Kaladaksha, then Surasundari,
Vibhrama, Vahaka, Vira, Vikala, Koraka, Kavi, Simhanada, Mahanada, Sugriva, Markata, Shatha,
Bidalaksha, Bidalasya, Kumari, Khechari, Bhava, Mayura, Mangala, Bhima, Dvipavaktra, Kharanana,
Matangi and Nishachara, Vrishagraha, Vrikanana, Sairibhasya, Gajamukha, Pashuvaktra, Mriganana,

Thus the divine thousand names of the Goddess Lalita have been declared, granting success in all aims and the fruit of the four goals of life.
Whoever recites this daily at dawn with a pure mind becomes a yogi, a knower of Brahman, a sage, a yogi of Shiva and a knower of the Self.
For one who recites it twice, long life, health and wealth, delighting the world and winning over women and kings
surely come to that practitioner without fail. By reciting it three times, the whole universe comes under a man's control.
By four recitations whatever he wishes surely bears fruit constantly; fit for applications, he becomes a protector of the world.
By five recitations men, women, kings, gods and creatures serve this practitioner, their minds fixed on the Goddess.
By six recitations the practitioner becomes one with her, and his successes arise very soon by the grace of the goddesses.
By seven recitations enemies, diseases, black magic and epilepsy are destroyed; by eight a man becomes able to restrain and favour kings.
By nine recitations, shining like Manmatha, he stirs the earth; one should recite it ten times daily for success in speech, prosperity and beauty.
By eleven recitations all riches come and the world becomes subject to him; by twelve, with the siddhis, a mortal becomes like Hara in all directions.
By thirteen recitations a man becomes victorious and happy everywhere; by fourteen, every wish is attained and there is good fortune everywhere.
By fifteen recitations a man escapes all misfortunes; by sixteen a man becomes Maheshvara himself,
able to create, protect and dissolve the universe. Whoever recites it for a mandala of forty days, or for a month, with whatever intention,
obtains that very thing, truly, as Shiva has said. Thus, O brahmin, I have told you, based on the worship of the enclosures of the Nityas,
the thousand names, able to accomplish the mind's desire.
And if one worships her for a month with the nine gems, freed from the mass of all sins one sees her with one's own eyes.
If one worships the Goddess for a month with fragrant garments, one is freed from the mass of sorrows arising from sins and other causes.
Contemplating oneself as the Goddess's form, with the chakra and the Shaktis all around, and worshipping with the flowers of the sense objects, one becomes one with her.
Each of the sixteen Nityas has her lunar day in order; on that day one should perform her worship, japa, oblation and the rest.
Ghee, sugar, milk, cakes, bananas, honey, jaggery, coconut, parched rice, sesame and curd,

To the first, Lalita, all these should always be offered; one should offer them into the fire and give them to people as well.
The medicine named by the letters of each vidya, in its proper measure, should be ground and made into pills, and with them one should accomplish everything.
